Introduction  
 
Thank you for purchasing this machine.  
Always be sure to read this manual carefully first, in order to use the machine 
functions properly and safely.  
 
 
 
This machine manual is divided into the following sections.  
• Operation Manual  
This manual describes the operation procedure for the machine.  
• Installation Manual  
This manual describes the machine’s installati on procedure and 
inspections.  
• Programming Manual  
This manual provides a program description.  
 
Brother is not responsible or liable for accidents that occur during special 
machine use or handling that does not follow the general safety usage 
guidelines.  
Keep this manual for future reference.  
Attach this manual to the machine if it is resold.  
Contact the nearest Brother sales office or Brother approved service dealer if 
this manual or the safety labels are damaged, lost or missing. (Charges apply)  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The re -exporting and resale of this machine is regulated by Japan’s export laws and 
regulations in accordance with international export management.  
When exporting, permission from the exporting country’s government and/or from the 
Japanese government may be required.  
Contact a Brother Industries dealer in advance before re- transferring, reselling or 
re-exporting this machine.  
 
Copying and reprinting all or part of the content in this manual without permission is illegal.  
The content of this  manual may be changed without prior notice. 
Brother has taken steps to ensure this manual is accurate and complete. However, if you notice 
or suspect that there is an error, please contact the nearest Brother sales office or Brother 
approved service dealer.  
We provide source code to customers who wish to use GPL or LGPL software. Contact Brother 
for further details. (A separate fee and service charge applies.)  
Ethernet is a registered trademark of Xerox Corp. in the U.S.A.  Make sure you use a router or 
firewall when connecting your Brother machine to the Internet to protect it against unauthorized 
access from the Internet

How to Read This Manual  
 
This manual is divided into the following sections.  
(1) Overview  ------ A summary of the content is provided for the corresponding section.  
 
(2) Warning  -------- A warning is provided for any hazards that could potentially cause serious bodily 
injury, death or damage to the machine.  
The hazards are described in the following order.  
(2-1) Hazard level  
(2-2) Type of hazard  
(2-3) Potential damage 
(2-4) Safety directions to avoid danger  
 
(3) Operation procedure --- The procedure describes how to operate each function.  
 
(4) Screen shot  --- A screenshot is inserted into places to highlight certain points in the operation 
procedure. The screens hot messages are shown at an approximate position and may 
differ slightly from the actual position of the line or column. The same applies to the 
font. 
 
(5) Illustration ---- Illustrations, such as explanatory drawings, diagrams that show the dimensions, 
positioning, ranges, figures or configurations, are used in certain places where a 
written explanation alone may be hard to understand.  
 
 (2) Warning  (3) Operation procedure  
1.3 Take the necessary steps to ensure 
safe operation  1.3.1 Before starting operation  
Review the following items before starting 
operation.  
(1) Turn the main power breaker handle on the control 
box door to the OFF position.  
Do not touch the primary power and terminal for the 
main power breaker because it has a high voltage.  
(2) A sign must be posted to warn others that work is 
in progress.  
(3) Do not let others approach the machine or the 
moving parts on the machine.  
(4) Make sure that there are no unnecessary objects 
around the machine.  
        WARNING  
You may break or fracture your foot 
if you drop a heavy object on it.  
Therefore, use safety footwear when 
lifting or carrying heavy objects.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 2 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 1.1 Outline  
The following four functions are available in program edit mode.  
 
1. Creation and modification of NC type program  
2. Creation and modification of c onversation type programs  
3. Display of registered program No., deletion, copy and check of the programs.  
4. I/O of programs and data to/ from an external unit  
5. Preprocessi ng for NC program  
 
Operation method is as follows.  
 
(1) Press the [EDIT] key (mode selection key ). 
(2) Press the menu No. and the [ ENT]  key, or move the cursor to the menu No. and press the 
[ENT]  key or press a function key. Each operation screen is displa yed. 
 
<Program edit menu > screen (NC language)  
 
 
<Program edit menu >screen (Conversation al language)  
 
 
When the [EDIT]  key is pressed while in memory operation, the operation temporarily stops or 
pauses (block stop). To edit or reference a program withou t stopping operation, press the [EDIT]  
key while pressing the [MEM] key.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 3 eCOM3OPDT1  1 1.2 Program Edit (NC)  
1.2.1 Program Edit 
This function is available only for  the NC language mode.  
Creation and modification of NC program are available.  
In addition , you can move  a program to a folder or create a folder.  
 
* For creation, correction, or storage of a program and creation of a folder, there are following 
capacity limits : 
• Total capacity of usable memory is about 1 28M bytes.  
• The total number of usable files and folde rs including NC  programs, conversational programs, 
databank s, and folders is 4096 files.  
 
Press [1] and then the [ ENT] key on the <Program edit menu> screen, or point the cursor at  the 
menu No. 1  and press the [ ENT] key to display the <Program list> screen . When the [ F1] 
(list/detail) key is pressed , the list display  and detail display  are switched . When the [ F2] (Sort) 
key is pressed, the order of the program s are sorted . 
 
[F0] (Date(ascending) ): Displays programs in the order from the oldest to the newest . 
[F1] (Date(descending) ): Displays programs in the order from the newest to the oldest.  
[F2] (Program No. (ascending )): Displays in the order from the smallest to the biggest.  
 Displays  the folder s in the alphabetical order of the folder 
names . 
[F3] (Program No. (descending )): Displays in the order from the biggest to the smallest.  
Displays the folders in the reverse alphabetical order of the 
folder names . 
[F4] (Comment(ascending) ): Displays in the alphabetical order of the character strings of the 
comme nt. 
 Displays the folders in the alphabetical order of the folder 
names . 
[F5] (Comment(descending) ): Displays in the reverse alphabetical order of the character 
strings of the comment.  
 Displays the folders in the reverse alphabetical order of the 
folder  names . 
Press the  [F6] key (Create folder) to display the screen for creating folders. The key cannot be 
pressed when the screen is already inside the folder.  
 
Example of the <D etailed program list> screen  
 
 
The details screen shows the program size, a description of block 1 in the program, the date and 
time the program was last updated, and the information is displayed according to the selected 
order.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 4 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 Seventeen programs can be display ed on one screen. Other programs can be displayed by pressing 
the [PAGE  DOWN ] or [PAGE UP] key. 
In addition , if there is a folder, a folder name is added with “/” after the name and display ed in the  
program number area and the program size area.  
 
Example  of the <Program list> screen  
 
 
On the <Program list> screen, program nu mber, program size, and up- date dates are displayed in 
the selected sort ed order.  
Sixty eight programs can be display ed on one screen. Other programs can be displayed by pressing 
the [PAGE DOWN ] or [PAGE UP] key. 
In addition , if there is a folder, a folder  name is added with “/” after the name and display ed in the 
program number area and the program size area.  
 
Program number at the center below the title is the program edited last time.  On the line below that, 
a folder name ( current folder ) display ed in the present list is display ed. 
 
Enter the program No., or point the cursor at  the program No. to be edited, and press the [ ENT] 
key. 
If a program number which is not in the NC  is input and the  [ENT] key is press ed, it is an edit of a 
new program . 
After movin g the cursor to the folder and pressing the [ENT] key, the screen changes to the 
selected folder and shows a list of items in that folder.  
 
(Note) Even if folder name is entered and the [ENT] key is pressed, the screen 
cannot change to the folder screen.  
 
During memory operation, the program that is running is highlighted in green.  
If a program is protected and cannot be edited, that program is highlighted in grey.  
* Refer to the “1.4 Directory display” for further details on currently running programs and 
protected programs that cannot be edited.  
 
The edit program number and the memory operation program number are independent numbers. 
But if the < Set same number to edit/memory operation programs > of the user parameter is set < 1: 
Yes>, they can be accorded i ncluding the folder.  
For instance, if the memory operation mode is set when the edit program number is 1 000, the 
memory operation program number becomes 1 000. In addition , if the edit mode is set when the 
memory program number is 2000, the edit program num ber becomes 2000.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 5 eCOM3OPDT1  1 (Note 1 ) The program number s 9000 - 9999 cannot be used . 
(Note 2) A description of block 1 in the program is displayed on the <Detailed 
program list> screen. The user can insert comments using the 
control -out and control -in codes (“(”, “)”). This makes the overview 
helpful because the user does not have to look inside the program to 
check the description. Note, there is a 60 character limit for the 
description that is displayed in the <Detailed program list> screen.  
 
Folder  creation screen (Example of a list screen ) 
 
 
If the <Program list> screen  or the < Detailed program lis t> screen  display s a root folder , press the 
[F6] (Create folder ) key to display  the Folder creation screen . 
 
If a folder name to create is input and the  [F1] (Creat e) key is pressed , a new folder is creat ed and 
returns to the previous screen . 
Press the [ F0] (Back ) key  to return to the  previous screen  without creating a folder . 
 
A folder name can have up to 8 alphanumerical characters and a period . 
In addition, the fold ers that can be created at the machine can extend to 2 levels including the root 
directory.  (You cannot creat e another folder in a folder which has already been created. ) 
 
You cannot create a folder name like an already esisting folder , name s (O0000- O9999)  in an NC  
program, or a name in a conversational  program . If it is tried to create , the operator message 
<<This is a n unusable folder name >> appears .

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 6 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 <Edit> screen  
 
 
 
 
• Edit can be performed in the screen mode (mode which displays the editing programs  to 
modify directly).  
• The end of block code (EOB ) is indicated as “;”. 
• The cursor indicates the position to start editing.  
• One screen can disp lay max. 24 lines.  
• The block number in a block where the cursor exists is highlighted in a gray background.  
 
The maximum size of an editable program is 20M bytes. 
• 163840 blocks if a full characters are input in a block  (127 characters + EOB) . 
• 20971518 blocks if all the block s are filled with only EOB.  
 
If a program over 20M  bytes  is tried to be edited , the operator message <<Memory overflow >> 
appears to disable editting . 
In addition , if it exceeds 20M bytes  during editing, the operator message <<Editting area 
exceeded >> appears to disable  addition of a character . Divide the program.  
 
When the program size e xceeds the program load size, or when the program size including all sub 
programs being called exceeds the program load size, the program runs in extended memory 
operation mode during operation.  
When the program load size is the size that is selected in th e user parameter (switch 1) <Program 
load size>.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 7 eCOM3OPDT1  1 1.2.1.1  Basic Operations  
1. Deletion of charact er 
Press the [DEL]  key. 
The character pointed by the cursor is deleted by one character.  The remaining of the block 
after the cursor is moved to the left by o ne character.  
 
If the cursor is positioned on the end of block (EOB) code “;”, then that block and the next one 
merge and become one block. The entire next block shifts to the cursor position.  
However, if the number of characters of the connected block exceeds 127 characters, the 
operator message <<Too many characters >> appears to disable deletion.  
 
Push the [BACKSPACE] key. 
One character right before the cursor position is deleted . All content for that block including 
the cursor shifts 1 character space to  the left.  
 
If the cursor is at the head of a block , the block and the next block are connected into one 
block and the entire next block moves to the end of the before block . 
However, if the number of the characters in a block after connection exceeds 127 characters, 
the operator message <<Too many characters >> appears to disable deletion.  
 
2. Insertion of character  
Insertion is available as long as the [INS]  LED is lit on.  
When any of the alphabetical keys, numerical keys or symbol keys is  pressed at this time, the 
character specified by the keys is  inserted before the character pointed by the cursor. The 
cursor and the rest of the characters are moved to the right by one character.  
* The insertion input mode  is the prompt when a program edit starts.  
 
3. Overwriting of character  
Press the [INS]  key and turn off the LED. The o verwriting mode is valid as long as the LED is 
lit off.  
When any of the alphabetical keys, numerical keys or symbol keys is  pressed, the character 
pointed by the cursor is  replaced by a new character.  
When the cursor is at “;” the character s specified by the pressed key are inserted before this 
symbol as in the insertion mode.  
After overwriting is finished, press the [INS]  key again. The LED is lit on and the insertion 
mode becomes valid.  
 
4. Cursor shift  
The cursor is shifted by pressing the [ ↑], [↓], [←] and [→] keys.  
The cursor cannot move where there is no character. When the [ ←] key is pressed at the 
beginning of a block, the cursor moves over the “;” of the precedent block.  
When the cursor is at the bottom line of the screen, pressing the [ ↓] key scrolls the screen and 
moves the cursor to the next line or the next block.  
If the [↑] key pressed  at the top of a line , the scree n scrolls  down.  
 
If the [←] key is pressed while pressing the  [SHIFT]  key, the cursor moves to the head 
character of t he line.  
If the [→] key is pressed while pressing the  [SHIFT]  key, the cursor moves to the last 
character of the line (or “;” of the line ). 
 
5. Page change  
Screen changes by one page by pressing the [PAGE DOWN]  or [PAGE UP] key. 
After changing the page s, the cursor moves to the first character of the newly displayed page.  
 
The last line of the precedent page is displayed at the top of the next page before changing the 
pages.  The head  line of the precedent page is displayed at the bottom of the precedent pag e 
before changing the pages .

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 8 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 1.2.1.2  Search  
Character string of max imum 12 characters can be searched from the cursor position.  
 
 
[F0]……Search es forward . 
[F1]……Search es backward . 
[F4]……Enter character string and search  
[F7]……Exit search mode 
 
Input a se arch character into the search character string input area. The character string cannot 
include “;” (EOB).  
Search by pressing the [F0] (S earch forward) key  or [F1] (S earch backward ) key . 
The cursor moves to the head of the searched character string.  
If no designated character string is found, the operator message <<Data not found>> appear s but 
the cursor does not move.  
 
Under this condition, you can move the cursor and edit the program . 
 
After searching a character string, the specified character string is saved until turning off the 
machine.  
When you want to search the same character string continuously, press [F0] (Search forward) or 
[F1] (Search backward).  
When you want to change character string s to be searched, press [F4] (Search character string ) and 
you can input a desired character string.  
 
Press the [F7] (Cancel ) key to finish the search mode and return to the <Edit> screen.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 9 eCOM3OPDT1  1 1.2.1.3  Replacement  
Replace a character string that is 12 characters or less with another character string that is 12 
charact ers or less.  
 
 
[F0]……Replace 
[F1]……To search a downward candidate 
[F2]……To search an upward candidate 
[F3]……Enable or disable the replacement operation in a specific direction.  
[F4]……Replace all from the beginning of the program  
 
1. Input a character stri ng to be replaced and a new string character.  
When entering a character string for a <Search >, after pressing the [ENT] key, the cursor 
moves to the data input field to  enter data to < Replace>.   
After entering the character string to  <Replace> and pressing  the [ENT] key, the cursor moves 
to the data input field for a  <Search >. 
 
2. When pressing [F1] (Search forward) or [F2]  (Search backward), searching for the character 
string to be replaced begins from the cursor position forward or backward. When pressing the 
[F4] (Replace from top) key, searching downward from the head of the program is performed. 
The cursor moves to the beginning of the searched character string. If there is no  character 
string to be  replaced, the operator message <<Data not found>> appe ars to return to the 
<Edit> screen.  
 
3. When pressing [F0] (Replace) key, the character string is replaced with the new one.  
When pressing [F1] (Search forward) key, replacement is not performed and the cursor moves 
to the beginning of the next candidate c haracter string. If there is no  character string to be 
replaced, the operator message <<Data not found>> appears to return to the <Edit> screen.  
When pressing the [F2] (Search backward) key, replacement is not performed and the cursor 
moves to the beginnin g of the next candidate character string. If there is no  character string to 
be replaced, the operator message <<Data not found>> appears to return to the <Edit> screen.  
If the  [F3] (Replace all remaining ) key is pressed and a downward candidate is pressed , 
replacement is carried out downward from the cursor position. If an upward candidate is 
pressed, replacement is carried out upw ard in one go without checking.  
However, if replacement frequency exceeds 1000 times, the operator message <<Replacement  
perfor med too many times >> appears and the replacement finishes to return to the <Edit> 
screen.  
 
The current character string (character string to be replaced) and the new character string are saved 
until these are changed or turning off the power.  
If the size exceeds 20 M bytes due to replacements or if the number of characters in a block 
exceeds 127 characters, the operator message <<Editting area exceeded >> or <<Too many 
characters >> appears and the replacement process is held to return to the <Edit> screen.

 1.2.1.4  Jump 
When the [F0] (Jump to top ) key is pressed, the cursor jumps  to the head of a program. If the  [F1] 
(Jump to end) key is pressed, the the cursor jumps  to the end of the program . When entering a 
block number and pressing the [ENT] key, the curs or jumps to the first character of the specified 
block.  
 
 
[F0] Jumps to the head of a program  
[F1] Jumps to the end of a program  
[F7] Returns to the <Edit> screen without jumping anywhere  
 
If a block number larger than the total number of the blocks is in put, the cursor jumps to the  end of 
a program .

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 11 eCOM3OPDT1  1 1.2.1.5  Copy  
This is a function to coy a part of program to a different part. 
 
1. Point  the cursor at the first character  you want to copy . 
2. Press the [F4] (Copy) key.  The title displays < Copy >. 
3. Move th e cursor to the character that comes after the last character to be copied. All characters 
to be copied will be displayed in reverse.  
4. Press the [F0] (Copy) key. The part that is displayed in reverse is saved.  The title returns to 
<Edit>.  
5. Point the cu rsor at the part you want to copy.  
6. Press the [F5] (Paste) key. The taken characters are inserted before the character specified by 
the cursor.  
 
Example of < Copy > screen  
 
 
The maximum size of memory for copying or cutting -off is 20 M bytes.  
 
1.2.1.6  Paste 
The group of characters that are selected for copy or cut operations is saved. That content is saved 
until a new copy or cut operation is performed or the power to the machine is turned OFF.  
The content can be called for and inserted in the character before the cursor position for any 
number of times by pressing the [F5] (Paste) key.  
 
This function is used in the following cases : 
• Restor ation  after cutting  
• Mov ing a specified character group to another place  
• Copying a specified character group to sev eral places  
• Copy ing or moving  a specified part of a program to another program

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 12 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 1.2.1.7  Cut 
This is a function to cut a part of a program per character. The cut characters can be saved and 
pasted to another place.  
 
1. Point the cursor at the first chara cter to be cut.  
2. Press the [F6] (Cut) key. The screen displays < Cut>. 
3. Point the cursor at the precedent character next to the last character to be cut. All the 
characters to be cut are highlighted.  
4. Press the [F0] (Cut) key. The part that is display ed in reverse is cut and saved. The title returns 
to <Edit>.  
5. When pasting the cut character to another place, move the cursor to the place to be pasted.  
6. Press the [F5] (Paste) key.  The cut character is inserted to the character before the cursor 
position. 
 
Example of < Cut> screen  
 
 
The maximum size of memory for copy ing or cuting -off is 20 M bytes.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 13 eCOM3OPDT1  1 1.2.1.8 Insertion of Automatic Sequence Number  
If EOB  is input, the sequence number is automatically inserted.  
The value of the sequence number is set w ith the sequence number of the block, where EOB is 
input, added with the user parameter < Automatic sequence insertion increment >. When the block 
where EOB is input does not have a sequence number, the value of the sequence number is  set 
with the user param eter <Automatic sequence insertion increment >. 
 
To switch the  [F7]( Start auto sequence insertio n / End auto sequence insertion)  key 
 
 
1.2.1.9  Search for Block 
The cursor jumps to the currently operating block by pressing the [F1] (Search for block) key 
when the editing program is the currently operating program on the <E dit> screen of the operating 
program.  
If the program in editing differs from the program in operation or is not in operation , the operator 
message <<Data not found >> appear s and the cursor does not move.  
 
If there is no “Search for block” in the function display, change the functions  by pressing [>>] 
(next function) key.  
 
 
The block number pointed by the operation pointer is indicated in a black background.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 14 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 1.2.1.10  Menu Programming  
Menu programming is the function enable to make NC program by inputting numerical values 
according to the menu.  You don’t need to remember G/M codes.  
For details, refer to “ 1.2.3 Menu programming”.  
 
1.2.1.11  Edit Finish  
When the [F0] (Completion  mode ) key is pr essed on the p rogram edit screen, the edit finish check 
mode is called and the screen to select a con dition for finishing is called.  
You can save a program for  finishing or continue editing.  
If an edited program is in operation, the message < A program is c urrently running. Are you sure 
you want to change? > appears.  
 
(Note) If the edited program exceeds 2 M bytes  and is in extension memory 
operation , the message <End editing after operation is completed. > 
appears. Consequently, neither storing nor overwriti ng becomes 
available.  
In addition, if the edited program is in drawing and the program in 
drawing exceeds 2 M bytes, the message <Quit editing after drawing is 
completed. > appears. Consequently, neither storing nor  overwriting 
becomes available.  
 
Screen  to check editing of a program during operation  is finished  
 
 
1. [F0] (Cancel w/ saving chan ges) key 
Editing finish es when the  edited conten t is saved.  
The screen returns to the <Program list> screen.  
However, if a program in extension memory operation is ed ited or a program larger than 2 M 
bytes  in drawing is edited, you cannot push the [F0] (Cancel w/ saving changes ) key.  
2. [F3] (Cancel w/o saving changes ) key  
Edited contents are invalidated.  
The screen returns to  the <Program list> screen.  
3. [F6] (Overwr ite save) key  
The contents ever edited are overwritten in a file and the screen returns to the edit status.  
However, if a program in extension memory operation is edited or a program larger than 2 M 
bytes in drawing is edited, you cannot push the  [F6] (Overwrite save ) key . 
4. [F7] (Edit mode) key 
Returns to the editing status .

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 15 eCOM3OPDT1  1 1.2.2  Program Edit in Memory Operation (Edit During 
Operation)  
Programs are editable during a memory operation without stopping the operation . 
 
1.2.2.1  To Edit a P rogram not in Oper ation or a New 
Program  
1. Press  the [EDIT]  key while pressing the  [MEM]  key. 
The LED s of the  [MEM]  and [EDIT] keys go lit.  
2. Set a program number other than the one currently executed  to create a new program or reedit  
a current  program.  
 
(Note ) Unless the  [MEM]  key is pressed in 1 above, the mode becomes the 
program edit mode a nd the memory operation stops.  
 
1.2.2.2  To Edit a Program in Execution  
1. Press the  [EDIT] key while pressing the [MEM]  key. The LEDs of the [MEM]  and [EDIT]  
keys go lit . 
2. Set a pr ogram number in operation to enable editing . Here, the message <<Running 
program >> appears.  
 
If the user parameter < Program edit start position during operation  > is set as < 1: Pointer >, the 
cursor moves to the operation pointer pos ition when the editing started.  
The block number of the operation pointer is display ed in a black background.  
 
If the user parameter < Save when mode of current program is changed > is set < 1: Overwrite save> , 
the message <Perform overwrite save by mode switching. > appears in the teaching area.  
 
3. If the [F0] (Completion  mode ) key is pressed after editing a program, the message <A 
program is currently running.  Are you sure you want to change? >appears for confirmation . 
4. Press the  [F0] (Cancel w/ saving changes ) key to save the ed it content.  
 
(Note ) Unless the [MEM] key is pressed in 1 above, the mode becomes the 
program edit mode a nd the memory operation stops.  
 
The saved program in operation is reflected in memory operation after the operation finishes.  
 
If any of the [MANU], [MDI], [MEM], and  [EDIT] keys is pressed while a program in operation 
is being edited and the modes are changed, the user parameter < Save when mode of current 
program is changed > is set < 1: Overwrite save >, the edited content is overwriten and saved in a 
file.

Chapter 1 Program E dit 
 
2020/03/02  1 - 16 eCOM3OPDT1  1 
 1.2.3  Menu Programming  
Menu programming is the function enable to make NC program by inputting numerical values 
according to the menu.  You don’t need to remember G/M codes.  
If there is no menu programming in the function display , press the next menu ke y [>>](next 
function) to switch the function.  
 
1. Press [F2] (Menu programming)  key to call the Menu programming screen.  
2. Press [F1] (G code) key or [F2] (M code) key . 
3. Move the cursor to the G/M code to be made and press [ENT]  key.

2020/03/02  2 - 209 eCOM3OPDT2 -3 2 2.6.1.1  Edit Screen  
Selecting <External I/O signal > on the < Data bank menu>  screen displays the Edit screen for 
external I/O signal s. 
 
 
The previously displayed category is displayed .  By p ressing the function key , the displayed 
category  can be switch ed to another one . 
 
The list of external signals to be displayed in  the lower section of the screen for the category 
<External input signal > or <External output signal>  can be switch ed to the next page by pressing 
the [F7] (Next menu) key.  
 
* The s ignals shown in red signify those which cannot be supported in the current language 
mode (Conversation/NC).  
* The terminals whose terminal number is grayed out signify those which are not connected 
(cannot be recognized).  Although signals can be set to such termin als, however, please note 
that signals are not input/output to/from these terminals.

2020/03/02  2 - 210 eCOM3OPDT2 -3 2 2.6.2  How to Edit 
2.6.2.1  Locating the Cursor  
Locate the cursor at the  item to be changed using the cursor key.  
Search can be used to immed iately locate the cursor at a desired “terminal block” or “E xternal 
alarm.”  Enter a terminal block number (0: standard terminal block, 1 to 64: extended terminal 
blocks 1 to 64) in the input area, enter an external alarm number, and press the [F6] (Search ) key.  
Then the cursor is located at the designat ed number.  
 
2.6.2.2  Data Input  
1. Display the category to be changed.  
2. Locate the cursor at the item to be changed.  
3. Enter a value in the input area and press [ENT].  
For the  <External input signal > and <External output signal >, enter the number of the external 
signal to be allocated to the terminal.  
 
This inputs the value at the cursor position and moves the cursor to  the next item.  
 
* As to < 900:PLCX000-00F > through <961:PLCX3D0-3DF>  in <External input signal > and 
<900:PLCY000 -00F > through <961:PLCY3D0-3DF > in <External output signal >, set them 
for every 16 terminals collectively  at a time . 
When s etting them, they are set to 16 terminals including the one with the terminal number at 
the cursor position ( NO.**0 0 to 15 or NO.**16  to 31) collectively at a time.  Please note that 
the preset signals are overwritten.  
 
When entering the number of other signal in the input area with the cursor located at any of the 16 
terminals (N O.*00 to 15 or NO.*16 to 31) to w hich signals <900:PLCX000-00F > through 
<961:PLCX3D0- 3DF>  or <900:PLCY000-00F > through <961:PLCY3D0-3DF>  are set  and 
pressing [ENT] , only the signal at the cursor position  is set and the settings for the other 15 
terminals  are deleted.

2.6.2.4  Overlapping Input Terminal Check  
The values set on each screen for one setting item are only valid for 1 terminal on the following 
screens: external input signal (stan dard terminal block, extension terminal block 1 to 64), the 
PROFIBUS DP slave (PROFIBUS DP → NC )/status, , the DeviceNet slave (DeviceNet → 
NC)/status and the CC-Link slave RY/RWw (CC -Link → NC)/status screens.  If the same value is 
overlappingly  set to mul tiple setting item s, only the first set terminal  is made valid  in the order 
shown below and the subsequent setting items are treated as “no setting” . 
• Smaller terminal number of standard terminal block s 
• Smaller terminal number of extended terminal block s 
• Terminal that is displayed on top in the PROFIBUS DP slave status  
• Small terminal numbers for the PROFIBUS DP slave (PROFIBUS DP → NC)  
• Terminal that is displayed on top in the DeviceNet slave status  
• Small terminal numbers for the DeviceNet slave (DeviceNet → NC)  
• Terminal that is displayed on top in the CC-Link sla ve status  
• Small terminal numbers for the CC -Link slave (RY/RWw (CC-Link → NC))  
 
When p ressing the [F5] (Overlapping terminal check) on any of the input signal screens , check for 
overlappingly set terminal s is performed .  (Search the files being edited.)  
When there are no overlapping terminal s, <Check OK > is displayed in the teaching area.  
When there is any overlapping terminal, the names of the signals to which  the terminal is 
overlappingly  set, the terminal block  in which the overlapping terminal  is placed and the terminal 
number of the overlappig terminal are displayed as shown below.  
• When there are multiple overlapping terminals, thery are displayed in serial order of their set 
numbers to the extent that they can be displayed.  
• When there are overlap ping terminals too many to be displayed in the display area, they are 
not displayed.  
• Overlapping terminal check is performed also for the terminal blocks not connected to the 
machine.  
• When the CM PCB is an intelligent device station, the terminal name that is duplicated 
appears as follows.  (Refer to the screen below for a display example of RWw.)  
When Rx is duplicated: CM Rx+*** (Note 1)  
When RWr is duplicated: CM RWr+*** (Note 2)  
(Note 1)  *** refers to a code between 000 and 3F F. 
(Note 2)  *** refers to  a code between 000 and 07F.

2.7.1  Outline  
Set p arameter s for external input /output communication . Make setting in accordance with the 
connected device.  
 
Communication parameters are divid ed into the following categories.  
Category name  Description  
<Serial port > Sets the communication parameters for serial port.  
<Ethernet/FTP > Sets the communication parameters for Ethernet and FTP.  
<Memory card > Sets the communication parameters for memor y card.  
<Auto notification function>  Set the parameter for the auto notification function.  
 
2.7.1.1  Edit Screen  
Selecting <Communication parameter > on the <Data bank menu > screen displays the 
communication parameter edit screen.  
 
 
Displays the previousl y displayed category. Category can be switched over by pressing a function 
key. 
 
2.7.2  How to Edit 
2.7.2.1  Data Input/ Output  
1. Display the category that includes the item to be changed.  
2. Locate the cursor at the item to be changed.  
3. Enter a value in the input area and press the [ENT] . 
This inputs the value at the cursor position and moves the cursor to the next item.  
 
* For details of the items, see para. 2.7.3 or later.  
 
2.7.2.2  Data Deletion  
When the cursor is located at an item that is deletable, <Can be deleted > is displayed.  
1. Display the category that includes the item to be deleted.  
2. Locate the cursor at the item to be deleted.  
3. Press the  [Delete] key. 
This deletes the value at the cursor position.  
 
2.7.2.3  Ending Editing 
Upon completion of the settings, press the [F0]  (End mode) key to end the editing.  
For how to end editing, refer to “ 2.1 General Outline of Data Bank” . 
(Note)  When communication is in progress, a reset may be requested when 
exiting editing depending on the item(s) that was c hanged. In this 
situation, press the [RST] key after the communication has finished in 
order to reflect the parameter change.

2020/03/02  2 - 267 eCOM3OPDT2 -3 2 13. Initial life/life end  
Locating the cursor at the “Initial life/life end ” enables the life unit and the initial life/life end 
to be set.  
 
* Dependin on the setting for the <Tool life counting method> in the User parameters, the 
item name changes to either “Initial life ” or “Life end .” 
• When the value of the <Tool life counting method> is set to “ 0: Type 1, ” the tool life 
management is performed by counting down, and the item name is displayed as 
“Initial life ”. 
• When the value of the <Tool life counting method> is set to “1: Type 2, ” the tool life 
management is performed by counting up, and the item name is displayed as “ Life 
end”. 
 
Life unit is selectable from the following four units.  
Set value  Unit Description  
1: Not counted  None  Tool life management is not perf ormed  
“1: Setting to “1: Not counted,” the “Tool life/life end” 
is displayed as “Life warning” and “**” is displayed in 
the “Life” item.  
2: Time  Min Tool life management is performed in time (in the unit 
of minute).  
As the cutting travel is performed for one minute, the 
tool life is subtracted/added.  
3: Drilled holes  Holes  Manages the tool life based on the number of holes 
drilled.  
When 1 hole is drilled in a drilling job, or when a 
motion call is executed for 1 job, the count for the tool 
life is added o r subtracted accordingly.  
4: Workpieces  Number of 
workpieces  Tool life management is performed in workpieces.  
At the end of operation, the tool life of the tool with 
which cutting travel has been done is subtracted/added.  
 
Setting the tool life unit goes  to the setting of the initial life/life end.  
For the initial life/life end, st the initial value/end value of the tool life.  
For the initial life, setting a initial life sets the same value for the tool life.  
For the life end, setting a life end sets “ 0” for the tool life.  
 
14. Life warning  
For the life warning, set the tool life value at which the end of the tool life is warned.  
When the tool life reaches the value for the life warning, an alarm <<Tool life ending 
(****)>> (where the parenthesized value i s a tool number) is generated.  
Even after the generation of such an alarm, starting of memory operation remain enabled.  
* Setting the life warning to “0” in the counting -up type does not generate this alarm.  
15. Life 
Set the current value for the tool life . When the end of life is reached by subtracttion/addition 
as a result of machining, an alarm <<Tool life end (****)>> ( where the parenthesized value is 
a tool number) is generated. Upon generation of this alarm, starting of memory operation is 
prevented.  
 
* In the MDI operation, the tool life is not subtracted/added.  
* Only for the tools commanded in memory operation, tool life subtraction/addition and tool 
life check are performed. Thus when a tool change has been made through MDI operation 
during memory operation, tool life subtraction/addition and tool life check are not 
performed even after returning to the memory operation.  
* “End of life reached ” means that the tool life reaches “ 0” in the counting -down method or 
that the tool life reached the same as  the value set for the end of life in the counting -up 
method.  
* The tool life for the tool whose life end has reached can be initialized on the ATC tool 
screen.

2.9.2.8  Registering Tools with Auxiliary Code 
Tools can be registered with any of auxiliary codes 1 to 9. By giving auxiliary codes to tools 
beforehand, it is possible to designate the tool to be used where there are id entical tools.  
 
When specifying a tool type, giving a hyphen  [-] and any of auxiliary codes [1] to [9] following 
the tool type number and pressing the [ENT]  key adds the auxiliary code to the tool type number 
of the particular tool.  
 
In the example below, setting for a drill is performed with auxiliary code “1” given to the tool 
No.11.  
Locate the cursor at the “Tool” No.11, enter “2 -1” in the input area and press the [ENT]  key. 
 
 
By setting an auxiliary code in the tool list and setting a tool registered i n the cutting condition 1/2 
using the same auxiliary code beforehand, the tool with the auxiliary code is selected in tool 
allocation.  
 
2.9.2.9  End of Editing  
Upon completion of the setting, press the [F0] (End mode) key to end the editing.  
 
2.9.3 Editing during Operation  
An operator message <<Operating>> is generated and editing is prevented from being  ended.

2020/03/02  2 - 276 eCOM3OPDT2 -3 2 2.10 Tool pattern (Conversation)  
2.10.1 Outline  
Set the tool type to be used in the machining processes and their order of use.  Then, in tool 
allocation, the tools required for the respective machining processes are automatically selected 
according to the contents set here.  
 
Two types of tool patterns with or without chamfering can be set for each machining process.   
 
Normally tools are automatically selected according to the default tool pattern set at shipment. 
However, some machining process may require pattern to be changed.  
 
2.10.1.1  Edit Screen  
Selecting the “ Tool pattern ” on the Data bank menu screen displays the edit screen for tool 
patterns.

2.10.2.1  Locating cursor  
Locate the cursor at the item to be changed using the cursor key.  
Pressing the [F1] (Previous pattern) or the [F2]  (Next pattern) key locates the cursor at the top of 
the previous or next machining process.  
 
2.10.2.2 Data Change  
Change the tool at the cursor position to another type of tool.  
1. Locate the cursor at the tool to be changed.  
2. Select a tool number from the tool types displayed below the input area, enter a value in the 
input area and press the [ENT] key. 
This overwrites the tool at the cursor position and loates the cursor at the next tool.  
 
2.10.2.3  Data Insertion  
Add a new data before the tool at the cursor position.  
1. Locate the cursor at the position to which the data is to be added.  
2. Press [INS] key. 
This displays “ *” and brings down the subsequent data by one.  
The tool which was set as the last tool in that machining process is deleted.  
3. Set the tool at the cursor position according to the procedure of “ 2.9.2.2 Data change. ” 
 
2.10.2.4  Data Deletion  
Delete the tool at the cursor position.  
1. Locate the cursor at the tool to be deleted.  
2. Press [DEL ] key. 
This deletes the tool at the cursor position and brings up the subsequent data by one.  
An asterisk “ *” is displayed at the end of that  machining process.  
 
2.10.2.5  Ending E diting 
Upon completion of the setting, press the [F0] (End mode)  key to end the editing.

3.1.1  Outline  
The program path can be confirmed by drawing it on the <Operation drawing> screen.  
The drawn path indicates the tool path.  
 
1. Press the [GRAPH] key. 
The <Ope ration drawing> screen appears.  
 
 
• Scale Displays the graphic scale.  
• Scale mark  A red line (one tenth of the width of the screen) with green digits is displayed 
at the top right of the screen. The green digits indicate the dim ensional 
relationship of the display to  the actual size of the object.  
 
There are two graphic modes: operation drawing mode and tool path simulation mode.  
 Outline  
Operation drawing  The operation path of programs stored for memory operation in the 
memory operation mode is drawn. This is available only in the memory 
operation mode.  
Drawing  during  operation: The movement path during memory 
operation, manual operation, or MDI operation is drawn.  
Tool path 
simulation  The operation path of the program is drawn  in any mode. Since any 
program number can be specified and executed, the graphic of the next 
memory operation program can be checked during the current memory 
operation.  
 
There are two graphic display modes: 2D (two -dimensional) and 3D (three -dimensional ). 
 Outline  
2D Displays the graphic when viewed from the plane set for [2D drawing 
plane]. When [3 -plane drawing] is selected, the screen is divided into 
four segments, and a view from one of three directions is displayed in 
three of these segments.  
3D Displays the graphic with the coordinate system set for [3D drawing 
plane] rotated by the angle set for [Horizontal rotation angle] or [Vertical 
rotation angle].

The tape run function operates the machine while reading the program from an external Input

Two types of tape run can be operated . 
1. One method is to read a program through serial port with the connect ed device set to “General 
communication device”.

2. Another method is to read a program t hrough USB port with the connect ed device set to 
“Memory card ”. 
(Hereinafter referred to as “ Tape run (Memory card) ”)

• In tape run mode, the pallet is loaded when operation is started although < Pallet loading > of

• Although <Program repeat > is set to <1: Repeat >, the operation stops at the point of program

• The files such as programs and data banks cannot be input or output during operation

Prohibited commands  
The following c ode cannot be used during tape operation.  
• Macro (WHILE DO to  END)  
Refer to “ 6.4 Control Function ” in the Programming Manual (NC language) for further details.  
 
 
Restricted commands  
There are restrictions for the following codes during tape operation.  
1. Sub program/macro program call (M98, M99, G65, G66)  
• Only those programs contained in the root folder in the machine can be called up.  
• Address P cannot be omitted when M 98 is specified.  
• M99 cannot be specified in the main program.  
• Address P cannot b e specified when M99 is specified.  
Refer to “Chapter 8 Subprogram Function” in the Programming Manual (NC language) for 
further details.  
2. Macros (GOTO to N)  
• If there is no specified sequence number in the data  between GOTO and the end of

 5.1 Overview  
5.1.1  Special Notes Bef ore Using Communication 
Function  
 
This product has communication functions, such as Ethernet. However it is not possible to 
connect directly to a telecommunication line (including public wireless LAN)  for 
telecommunication carriers (such as mobile communic ation carriers, fixed -line 
communication carriers, Internet providers, etc.). Make sure you use a router or firew all 
when connecting your Brother machine to the Internet to protect it against unauthorized 
access from the Internet.  
 
To avoid inadvertently l osing important data, we recommend regularly backing up the data 
in this product. If there is an accident, such as data being deleted due to a mistaken 
operation, data being corrupted due to a failure, or data being deleted and/or  falsified via 
remote oper ation from an external program on the network, the customer can shorten the 
recovery time and minimize the impact  on work by using backup data.  
A description of how to back up the internal data on this product is described later on.  
In addition, we recomme nd for the customer to save any data in a separate data storage 
device at the appropriate time, for example, when creating or making changes to data, such 
as data found in NC programs, conversation-language programs, internal PLC programs or 
in data banks.   
 
 
To customers using the FTP master station communication function: 
The FTP master station communication function allows customers to use this product to 
access an FTP server that is prepared separately by the customer. When using an FTP 
server, be sure to limit access to files used by this product, for example, by minimizing the 
range of access that is granted under the login name used on this product.  
 
 
Procedure to back up internal data for this product  
 
Items needed: Formatted memory card (USB memory ) 
1. Turn the machine breaker ON, and then turn the power ON.  
2. Insert the memory card into the memory card interface, which is under the machine’s 
operation panel.  
3. Change to maintenance mode.  
3-1. Change to <Program edit menu > screen.  
Press the [EDIT]  key. 
3-2. Change to <External I/O menu>  screen.  
Select  <External I/O> on the menu, and press  the [ENT]  key. 
3-3. Change to <Maintenance menu > screen.  
Select <Maintenance> on the menu, and press the [ENT] key. 
3-4. Make sure that <Connected>  on the bottom -right corner of the screen reads <Memory 
card>.  
If the connecti ng location is different, select <Change connection device>  and change  it to 
<Memory card>.  
4. Output  the internal machine  data to the memory card.  
4-1. Change to <Maintenance – Output all data > screen.  
Press the [F0] (Output all data) key. 
4-2. Output data to memory card.  
Press the [F2] (Output) key.  
After output is complete, it goes back  to the screen  before outputting.  
5. Remove memory card.  
 
Copy the internal machine data saved in the memory  card to the computer or other device to store 
it. If data is corrupted, this procedure can be used to restore the data by transferring and inputting 
the backup data.

5.2.2.2  Memory card  
NC has a USB interface fo r connecting memory cards. By inserting a USB memory or other 
adapter for USB- based recording media into the USB interface, these devices can  be used as an 
external storage for NC.  
Memory card for NC is a generic term for all these external storage devices  including USB 
memory sticks.  
 
* Precautions for use  
1. Only FAT16  and FAT32  memory card file formats are supported (number of files to be 
created, etc. depends on format).  
2. If write protect switch of a memory card is ON, input from the memory card to th e 
machine is possible but output from the machine is impossible.  
3. Security function o f memory card must be “released ”. The machine may not recognize the 
memory card.  
4. The access lamp of a memory card lights up when the machine accesses the card. Remove 
the card only after the necessary operations are completed and the access lamp goes off. If 
you remove the card during an access, the machine may not recognize the card until 
power is turned off and  then on next time.  
5. Even if the empty space of a media exceeds 2G  byte, the display on the screen remains 2G  
byte (maximum display value).  
6. The alarm << Multiple memory cards cannot be connected >> occurs if you connect more 
than one memory card.  
7. The data cannot be read correctly if you use commercial memo ry cards without first 
logically  formatting. Use them after logical formatting with the disc format of the 
machine.  
8. Be sure to take steps to back up important data on your computer because some memory 
cards are not necessarily designed for long term sto rage of data.  
9. Not all commercially available memory cards are guaranteed to function properly, and 
there are some cards with slower access speeds.  
When actually using a memory card, carefully check the operation before use.  
10. Memory cards that have no t been physically formatted cannot be formatted on this 
machine. Format the card on a PC.

5.3.1  Outline  
Communication is performed with th e machine as the slave station using  communication software 
having <NC communication  device protocol >, FTP client software, or browser software. 
Communication is possible even when the machine is running, subject to some restrictions 
depending on the type of communication.  
• File operation for programs, data banks, etc.  
• Operation of the machine 
 
5.3.1.1  Slave station communication from “NC COMM 
software”  
Serial port or Ethernet is used.  
Software for the master station must be created because a communicati on system unique to 
Brother is u sed. 
<Type2>  is used in the slave station communication regardless of the < NC communication device 
protocol (master) > setting. Slave station communication is impossible with <Type1>.  
 
In addition to file operation, operation  of the machine can be controlled using commands.  When 
using Ethernet, commands are transmitted as TCP/IP packet data.  
The machine becomes the server, waiting for connection establishment request from th e client at 
the port specified by the communication parameter <Port No.> . 
When the communication parameter  <Restrict Ethernet access> is set to <1: Yes> , the access 
becomes restricted. Use a temporary access command.  
 
Even if  <Restrict Ethernet access> is set to <1: Yes>  when using the serial port , the access does 
not become restricted.  
 
Refer to the “5.5 Communication protocol ” for further details.  
 
5.3.1.2  Slave station communication from FTP client  
Ethernet is used. NC is the FTP server.  
The master station need not create special software because FTP protocols are used. Use any 
desired FTP client software.  
For the user name and password when connecting to the FTP, use the communication parameter 
settings: <Server user name>, <Password as server>, <Common  user name> and < Common 
password >. 
 
FTP allows file operation but cannot operate the machine by commands.  
(Note  1) When creating a new folder for the NC (FTP server side), sometimes a 
character string (Ex: [New folder] (2 byte character or more than 8 
characters), etc.) that is not allowed by the NC may be used to create the 
folder depending on the FTP client that is use d. 
In this situation, an error in the FTP protocol is triggered and the folder 
cannot be created.  
When creating a new folder for the NC (FTP server side) using the slave 
station’s communication from the FTP client, create a folder on the FTP 
client side ba sed on the rules (See below) for the folder level and name 
that are permitted by the NC. Then, copy the folder.  
• Up to 8 characters (alphameric characters and period) can be used for 
the folder name.  
• Up to 2 levels, including the route folder, can be cr eated. (A folder 
cannot be created inside another folder that is created.)  
• A name that already exists cannot be used for the folder name, such 
as another folder with the same name, a name being used inside the 
NC program (O0000 to O9999) or a name being used inside the 
conversation program.

 (Note 2)  Special response for delete (DELE) command  
When inputting (STOR) data that does not follow the file format, the NC 
returns an error response. However, depending on the FTP client being 
used, a delete (DELE) response may be issued as a second reply to the

the existing data in the NC may be deleted accidentally. Therefore, the 
following special response is used.  
A normal response is issued b ack to the delete (DELE) command for the

order to avoid deleting the existing data in the NC.

to “1”. I f the number of simultaneous connections on the FTP client 
software is set to “2” or greater, then the NC (FTP server side) may reject 
the connection and not transfer data properly.

 5.5.4  Ethernet Communication  
The following methods are available to communicate with the machine over Ethernet:  
• Slave station communication from “NC communication software”  
• Master station communication to < FTP server > 
• Slave station communication from FTP client  
• Slave station communication from a browser  
 
Network setting is required to communicate with the machine over Ethernet.  
Set communication parameters < Host name >, <Use DHCP >, <IP address >, <Mask bit >, <Default 
gateway >, <Auto acquisition of DNS server address> , <DNS server address 1 >, and <DNS server 
address 2 > according to your network environment.  
Contact your network administrator for any unknown points.  
In addition, when an unrelated device is connected to the machine on the same network, it causes 
an additional load on communications. Therefore, take the appropriate steps with the 
configuration.   
 
5.5.4.1  Slave station communication from  
“NC communication softwar e” 
• Protocol  
TCP/IP protocol is used for Ethernet communication.  
NC communication device protocol type 2 is encapsulated in the TCP/IP packet data. The 
machine runs as slave station and is a server in the TCP/IP protocol.  
 
• TCP port number  
The machine wa its for connection with the client at the TCP port number set to 
communication parameter < Port NO.> . The client should ask establishment of connection at 
this TCP port number.  
 
• Establishment and release of connection  
Connection is established / released using transmission of one pair of command and response 
of NC communication device protocol, type 2, as a session, in principle.  
When the client does not release the connection and no command arrives for a time period set 
by communication parameter  <Respons e monitoring time >, the server (machine) releases the 
connection. If you wish not to release connection from the server, set the <Response 
monitoring time > to <0>. 
• Restrict access  
Restrict access to this machine using communication protocol type 2 for an  NC 
communication device by setting  the communication parameter  <Restrict Ethernet access> to 
<1: Yes>.  
- All commands except a temporary access command  
When a temporary access command is issued, the access restriction is temporarily lifted. 
However, when the communication parameters <  Common user name  > and <Common 
password> are not set, the access restriction cannot be lifted.  
Temporary access continues from the previous session until the communication parameter 
<Access timeout period > elapses.  
If there are multiple release commands from the client side, access restriction is temporarily 
lifted only for the IP address on the client side when the temporary access command is finally 
issued.  
Refer to “5.5.9.3. Command details ” for further details on the temporary access  command.  
 
5.5.4.2  FTP communication  
General protocols are used and the description is omitted here.  
 
In the case of master station communication (the machine is an FTP client), connection is 
established with the “FTP server”  on the network according to communication parameters  <FTP

client >. 
 
For slave station communication (this machine is used as an FTP server) , use the communication  
parameter settings: <Server user name>, <Password as server>, <Common user name> and 
<Common password>  to connect on the client side .

This protocol applies to the case when type 2 is selected for the NC communication device at

Commands for not just data transfer but remote operations such as startup of memory operation for 
slave station and operation of external I/O signals are included.

C: Command; R: response  
One response of identifier R is always returned to each command of identifier C. The 
identifier of a response to a command is R, and the header of the same contents, excepting that 
a completion cod e is set, is echo -backed.  
c1-c3 Command type – 3 bytes  
f1-f4 Function – 4 bytes  
s1-s8 Message – 8 bytes  
r1-r2 Completion code – 2 bytes  
00 :Normally completed: other than 00: Abnormally completed  
 
Blank boxes appearing in the command header table hereafter  indicate a space.  
 
3. Data Section  
The portion starting with “LF” until “LF” of the footer appears is defined as the data portion.  
 
4. Footer (4 bytes)  
Footer is indicated by LFss% . 
“ss” indicates the checksum, which is represented by a 2 -digit decimal nu mber.  
It is calculated by adding all values from % in the header to the character before LF in the 
footer in decimal expression, than dividing it by decimal 16, and keeping the remainder.  
 
* % is the same as % in ISO and ASCII, and ER in EIA  
* LF is the sa me as LF in ISO, EOB in EIA, and CR+LF in ASCII.

Control method for auto notification function (when standard)  
 
*1 : When the SND_REQ is OFF, the ladder program prepares data for the auto notification and 
turns the SND_REQ to ON.  
*2 : The NC confirms that the SND_REQ is ON, an d after the SND_TRAN turns ON, the auto 
notification starts to send.  
*3 : After the NC sends the auto notification, the SND_TRAN is turned OFF, and the NC waits 
for a response from the notification destination.  
*4 : Once the NC receives a response from the notification destination, the error code is stored 
in D300, and the SND_RET is turned ON.  
*5 : The ladder program confirms that the SND_RET is ON, and the SND_REQ is turned OFF. 
(Check D 300 before SND -REQ is turned OFF.)  
*6 : The NC confirms that the SND_ REQ is OFF, and after clearing D 300, SND_RET is turned 
OFF.

Chapter 6 Data Protection  
 
2020/03/03  6 - 2 eCOM3OPDT6  6 6.1 Outline  
Six o peration levels are provided, at each of which data to be prevented from being changed and 
operation to be preven ted can be set. By making settings for  these operation levels , the machine is 
protected from erroneous operation s. 
Operation level  Operator  Setting  
Level 0 (low) User  Neither  password nor external input signal  
Level 1 User  Password or external signal  (LEVEL1 ) 
Level 2 User  Password or external input signal  (LEVEL2 ) 
Level 3 User  Password or external input signal  (LEVEL3 ) 
Level 4 User  Password or external input signal  (LEVEL4 ) 
Level 5 User  Password  
 
• Detailed settings can be registered for each dat a such as programs and data bank s at each 
operation level, and only the  data set to < Op. Enabled > at the current operation level  are 
permitted to  be edited . 
Detailed setting s can also be registered for keys, switches and screen displays.  
In some cases as s hown below, however, some data cannot be operated even if they are set to 
<Op. Enabled >. 
 
(1) When [DATA PROTECTION] switch is enabled ; 
(2) When editing is prevented  by the combination of external input signals (EDLOCK, 
PRLOCK, TLEDOK, UPEDOK, MPEDOK, ECEDOK, MGEDOK, M TEDOK, 
WPEDOK, MCEDOK, TPEDOK, THEDOK, CTEDOK and  DIROK);  
(3) When data protection is ON  for editing of program s #8000- 8999;  
(4) When <Parameter change> is set to < 0: Write -protected > on the I/O (version) screen for 
the editing of machine para meters;  
(5) When operation is prevent ed by the combination of external input signals (MDLOCK, 
KYLOCK, MODEOK);  
(6) When operation is p revented by PLC input signal s (KYLOCK1 to 6); or  
(7) When <Prevent rapid traverse override> , <Prevent cutting feedrateoverride> or <Prevent 
spindle override > is set to < 1: Yes > in the user parameters (switch 1).  
 
* Data can be changed  through the operaton using G10 or macro variables  even if the data is 
set to <Op. disabled>  
 
• If an operation set to <Op. disabled>  is attempted, an operator message <<No operation is 
possible under  the current level >> is generated.  
• Although input through communication is subject to restriction depending on the operation 
level, check input is possible . 
• For Input all data bank s or for Mainten ance (Input all data), data set to <Op. disabled>  are 
skipped. (An operator message <<Operation  disable data has  been skipped >> is generated.)

1. Select <Operation level>  from the I/O menu to display the Operation level screen.

• Enter the password into the data input field and press the [ENT]  key to set the current 
operation level.  
• Press the [F1] (Reset password) key, or press the [RST]  key, to turn < OFF>  all

• Turn ON the external input signal fo r a higher level than the current operation level.  
• The only valid keys on this screen are the alphanumeric keys, the [RST]  key and the [F1]

• If the password is entered incorrectly 5 times in a row, all < Password > settings are

• When the password is not set (factory settings) for levels 1 through 4, the operation level 
screen does not display when the power is turned ON. It starts up at the level when the 
power was turned OFF. (Excluding level 5)  
 
6.2.2  Setting by external input signal s 
As an alternative to entering a password for operation levels 1 through 4, the operation level can 
be set by entering the external input signals: “ LEVEL1 ”, “LEVEL2 ”, “LEVEL3 ” and “LEVEL4 ”. 
• Actual external input signal that  is input from the terminal  
• External input signal operation using the slave station command . 
• Exter nal input signal key.  
• PLC input signal . 
Turn OFF the external input signal to return to the previous operation level.  
 
* When multiple external input signals are turned ON, the highest operation level is enabled for 
the signals that are turned ON.  
 
6.2.3  Precautions  
• When the operation levels for the password and the external input signal  are both set, the 
highest valid operation level is enabled.  
• When the operation levels for the password and the external input signal  are both set, if the 
password is turned OFF, the operation level for the external input signal is enabled, or 
viceversa.  
• When the operation level is changed, the following operator mess age notification appears: 
<<Operation level setting (*) >>.

Passwords can be changed.  Please note that, however, only the passwords for the operation 
levels not higher than the current operation level can be changed.  Thus, to change a  password, 
frist set up the current operation level that is higher than the one  for which the password is to be 
changed.  4  to 10 alphanumeric characters (A to Z, 0 to 9) can be used for a password.  
 
6.3.1  Changing password  
1. One the operation level screen,  locate the cursor at the desired operation level for which the 
password is going to be changed, and press [F2] (Change  password) key.

7.2.1  Changing display language  
The text language on the machine unit display can be specified in the machine parameter <Display 
language>.  
The following languages can be selected and displayed: Japan ese, English, German, French, 
Chinese (simplified), Portuguese, Italian, Polish, Czech, Spanish and Korean.  
 
When the < Display language > has been changed in the machine parameter s, the display language 
is switch ed by restarting the machine.  
 
When the machi ne parameters are not provided or if the macine parameter file is destroyed, the 
display  is given in English. However, display language  can be selected  remporarily by a 
predetermined  operation at power -ON. 
For how to select temporary display language, refe r to “ Selecting temporary display language ” 
described later.  
 
In the data display area permitting entry of  character string, selecting a display language other than 
Japanese may cause garbled characters or incorrect display of characters, if Japanese is se t for the 
data of character string or if a file name or folder name in the connected device for external I/O is 
in Japanese.

 7.2.2  Selecting temporary display language  
When there are no machine parameters, or when the machine parameter file is corrupt, the display 
language is unknown and it is automatically set to English. Note, in this situation, the user can 
specify the display language temporarily using the startup operations.  
 
1. When the system is started up and the < Now Booting > screen appears, the following message 
is displayed in English for 20 seconds.  
 
 
2. Within the  20 seconds, press the function key for the desired display language  to be used 
temporarily . 
 
3. Then the screen is changed to be displayed in the selected display language.  
 
When no temporary display language has been selected within 20 seconds, the display is given in 
English.  
The setting of the temporary  display language is disabled by turning off the power supply.

http://Host Name (or IP address)
